title: Distances and light-time
summary: The astronomical unit, the speed of light, and why looking at the Sun means looking into the past.

badge.name: Light chaser
badge.text: You can turn a distance in space into a light travel time.

links.label: Measure the distance between two planets

steps.heading: Light has a speed
body: Light is fast, but not instant. In empty space it covers 299,792,458 meters every second, an exact value.

facts.text: The speed of light in empty space is 299,792,458 meters per second, exactly.

source.name: NIST CODATA 2022: speed of light in vacuum

checks.quote: speed of light in vacuum Numerical value 299 792 458 m s -1 Standard uncertainty (exact)

steps.heading: The astronomical unit
body: Kilometers get unwieldy in space, so astronomers also use the astronomical unit (au). One au is 149,597,870.7 km. Earth's average distance from the Sun is 1.00 au.

facts.text: Earth's average distance from the Sun is 1.00 au and Neptune's is 30.2 au.

steps.heading: Light time
body: Divide a distance by the speed of light and you get how long light takes to cross it.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to reach Earth, so when you see the Sun you see it as it was that long ago. It takes about 4.2 hours to reach Neptune.

facts.text: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to cross Earth's average distance from the Sun, and about 4.2 hours to reach Neptune.

questions.prompt: About how many minutes does sunlight take to reach Earth? Answer to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Earth's average distance divided by the speed of light is 8 minutes 19 seconds, about 8.3 minutes.

questions.prompt: About how many hours does sunlight take to reach Neptune?
questions.explanation: Neptune is about 30.2 au away on average, so light takes about 4.2 hours.

questions.prompt: If the Sun stopped shining right now, when would Earth go dark?

choices.explanation: Light needs time to travel, even this short distance.
The last light already on its way would still arrive.
That is too long: sunlight reaches Earth in minutes.

questions.explanation: Light takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to cover Earth's average distance from the Sun.
